items.body:
## Problem

The `google-gemini-cli` provider is **completely non-functional** for consumer-tier (free / Google AI Pro) users since Google sunset the Gemini CLI Code Assist endpoint on **June 18, 2026**.

This is not a feature request — it's a **service-affecting bug** that breaks a core provider for paying users.

## Current behavior

All Gemini models via `google-gemini-cli` fail:

| Model | Error | Frequency |
|-------|-------|-----------|
| `gemini-3.5-flash` | HTTP 404: "Requested entity was not found" | 100% |
| `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` | HTTP 400 (function call/response mismatch) or 429 (quota) | Intermittent |
| `gemini-3-pro-preview` | Same as above | Intermittent |
| `gemini-3-flash-preview` | Works intermittently via CLI, fails in desktop GUI | ~50% |

The **desktop GUI is completely unusable** with any Gemini model — every prompt errors out.

## Root cause

The `cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com` endpoint that `google-gemini-cli` routes through was shut down for consumer tiers on June 18, per Google's official announcement:

> June 18, 2026 — Gemini CLI and Gemini Code Assist IDE extensions stop serving requests for free and paid consumer tiers.
> Source: https://developers.googleblog.com/an-important-update-transitioning-gemini-cli-to-antigravity-cli/

## Existing PRs (both unmerged since May 20)

Two PRs have been open for **30+ days** since the sunset announcement, neither merged:

- **#29385** `feat/antigravity-cli-provider` — OPEN, unreviewed, last updated May 23
- **#29474** `feat/antigravity-native-oauth` — OPEN, has merge conflicts, last updated June 12

## Impact

- Users with Google AI Pro subscriptions **cannot use Gemini models through Hermes at all**
- The only workarounds are: switch to a different provider (Xiaomi MiMo), use third-party API proxies (fragile, ToS risk), or abandon Hermes for Gemini and go back to Antigravity CLI directly
- Issue #49099 was closed by the original author citing a personal workaround involving Agy CLI + "OpenRoute", but this does not fix the provider and is not accessible to users without `agy` installed

## Requested action

Merge one of the existing PRs or implement the Antigravity OAuth provider. This has been broken for 2+ days with no fix in sight despite PRs being available for over a month.

## Environment

- Hermes v0.17.0 (cf58f1a)
- Windows 10
- Provider: `google-gemini-cli` (2 OAuth accounts)
- Both CLI and desktop GUI affected

items.body:
Environment
  - OS: Windows 11
  - Hermes: Desktop app (Windows installer)
  - Docker Desktop with WSL2 backend
  - Config: terminal.backend: docker, terminal.cwd: /workspace, terminal.home_mode: auto

  What happens

  Hermes injects the Windows home directory (C:\Users\<username>) as the container working directory (-w flag), even though terminal.cwd is
  correctly set to /workspace in config.

  Error 1 (default config):
  docker: Error response from daemon: the working directory 'C:\Users\<username>'
  is invalid, it needs to be an absolute path

  Error 2 (after setting home_mode: container):
  bash: line 2: cd: C:\\Users\\<username>: No such file or directory

  The container is Linux-based — it cannot interpret Windows paths at all.

  Root cause (identified in source)

  In tools/environments/docker.py, lines 535–537:
  if cwd == "~":
      cwd = "/root"
  super().__init__(cwd=cwd, timeout=timeout)

  Only ~ is sanitized. When home_mode: auto resolves the Windows home directory (C:\Users\<username>), that path is passed through unmodified — then
  used both as the -w flag (line 867) and in the cd during init_session.

  Expected behavior

  When terminal.cwd is set to a Linux path (e.g. /workspace), that value should be used as the container working directory. Windows host paths
  should never be passed as the container cwd.

  Suggested fix

  Add a Windows path guard in docker.py after line 537:
  import re as _re_win
  if _re_win.match(r'^[A-Za-z]:[/\\]', cwd):
      logger.warning("Docker: Windows host path detected as cwd (%r) — falling back to /workspace", cwd)
      cwd = "/workspace"

items.title: [Bug]: Telegram group typing indicator persists and stream finalize delayed by ~10s
items.body:
### Bug Description

In Telegram group chats, after the Hermes bot finishes processing a request, the typing indicator persists for ~10 seconds after completion. Additionally, there is a ~10-second delay between the end of token streaming and the final formatted message (MarkdownV2/rich) appearing in the chat.

The typing indicator delay creates confusion: other group members think the bot has finished and begin discussing among themselves, then the bot sends more content.

Both issues also occur in DMs but are far more disruptive in group chats.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Trigger the Hermes bot in a Telegram group chat (via @mention or wake-word "hermes")
2. Watch the bot stream its response — typing indicator is active
3. Notice the streaming tokens stop arriving
4. Observe: typing indicator continues for ~10 seconds after the last streamed token
5. Observe: the final formatted message appears ~10 seconds after streaming ends

**Relevant config:**
- `display.platforms.telegram.streaming: true`
- `display.platforms.telegram.tool_progress: off`
- `telegram.require_mention: true`
- `telegram.mention_patterns: ["hermes"]`
- Telegram privacy mode: off (bot sees all group messages in whitelisted chat)

### Expected Behavior

- Typing indicator clears within 1-2 seconds of the response completing
- The formatted final message appears within <2 seconds after streaming ends

### Actual Behavior

- Typing indicator persists for ~10 seconds after the last streamed token
- Final formatted message appears after ~10 second delay

### Affected Component

- [x] Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

- [x] Telegram

### Debug Report

Universally reproducible — affects all Telegram group chats with streaming enabled. Does not require specific environment conditions to trigger. No errors appear in logs; this is a timing/perception UX issue.

### Operating System

macOS 26.5.1

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.17.0 (2026.6.19) · upstream 2ab09a6c

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

This is a timing/perception issue rather than a crash, so no traceback. The gateway log shows normal message delivery with no errors around the delay.

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

**1. Typing indicator persistence:**

`gateway/run.py` L9477-L9483 (try/except block) calls `stop_typing()`. However, Telegram's typing indicator is driven by a background asyncio loop `_keep_typing` (`base.py` L3160+) that refreshes `send_chat_action` every 2 seconds (`interval=2.0` at L3145). When `stop_typing` cancels the task, the loop must wake from its current sleep cycle (max 0.25s per `base.py` L3207) before responding to `CancelledError`.

Telegram's `send_typing` (telegram.py L5001-5030) is a one-shot `send_chat_action` call — there is no explicit "stop typing" Bot API endpoint. The base class `stop_typing` is a no-op (`base.py` L2601-2607). The `_keep_typing` `finally` block at `base.py` L3217-3219 also calls `self.stop_typing(chat_id)`, which is similarly a no-op for Telegram.

**Primary cause:** Telegram's client-side `send_chat_action` expires after ~5 seconds. Since the loop refreshes every 2s, the last refresh can complete its full 5-second client-side window before the indicator vanishes. This accounts for the majority of the ~10s delay. The remaining lag comes from stream finalization (see below) which runs after `_run_agent()` returns but before the final message is posted.

**2. Stream finalize delay:**

The finalize path for Telegram group chats (DMs differ — they support `sendMessageDraft`) is:

- `REQUIRES_EDIT_FINALIZE = True` (telegram.py L368) forces a `finalize=True` edit even when content is unchanged, to exit the streaming UI state.
- The final edit goes through `_try_edit_rich` (telegram.py, calls `editMessageText` with `rich_message` param via Bot API 10.1), not `_try_fresh_final` (which was explicitly reverted for Telegram in #46206 — `prefers_fresh_final_streaming` returns `False` at telegram.py L1064).
- The edit requires MarkdownV2 formatting conversion and a synchronous API round-trip to Telegram's servers.

The delay is the combination of: MarkdownV2 formatting of the full response + the `editMessageText` API call latency. Both are sequential and block final message delivery.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

**For typing:** Call `send_chat_action` with a short expiry immediately before cancelling the loop, or strip the typing indicator after the last API call rather than waiting for client-side expiry. Since Telegram has no explicit "stop typing" API, the practical fix is to stop the refresh loop earlier — ideally when the last token is streamed rather than when `_run_agent()` returns.

**For finalize:** The MarkdownV2 formatting is likely the main bottleneck for large responses. Consider formatting asynchronously or caching the formatted result. For the API round-trip, parallelize where possible (though `editMessageText` is inherently sequential with the final edit).

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Telegram groups currently have two interrupt-related problems:

**A. Non-triggering messages may reach the busy handler (possible bug):**

The user reports that after triggering the bot in a group, subsequent messages that do NOT contain the wake-word, do NOT @mention the bot, and are not replies to the bot, still appear to interrupt the running task.

Code analysis indicates `_should_process_message` (telegram.py L5850) should filter these out before they become events:
- Text handler filters at L5973: `if not self._should_process_message(msg): return`
- Command handler filters at L5990: `if not self._should_process_message(msg, is_command=True): return`
- Media handler filters at L6187: `if not self._should_process_message(update.message): return`

If non-triggering messages are indeed reaching `_handle_active_session_busy_message` (run.py L4122), this indicates a bug in `_should_process_message` under certain group/whitelist configurations, or a code path that bypasses the filter. This needs investigation.

**B. Cross-user interruption (design gap):**

Even when `_should_process_message` works correctly, any authorized group member can interrupt an active session by legitimately triggering the bot (e.g., User B @mentions the bot while User A's session is active). There is no per-user isolation — one user's triggering message interrupts another user's running task. This is the designed behavior of `busy_input_mode: interrupt` but is especially disruptive in multi-user groups.

Currently the only mitigation is global `display.busy_input_mode: queue`, which applies to all platforms and chat types (including DMs, where interrupt behavior is desirable).

### Proposed Solution

**For (A):** Investigate whether `_should_process_message` has a bug that allows non-triggering messages through when the chat is in an `allowed_chats` whitelist. Specifically check the interaction between `allowed_chats` and `require_mention` at telegram.py L5844-5863.

**For (B):** Add per-session or per-user busy handling in groups. Options:

1. **Adapter-level wrapping:** In `TelegramAdapter`, wrap the `set_busy_session_handler` callback to check the triggering user's ID against the session's active user. If the new message is from a different user than the one who triggered the current task, queue it rather than interrupting.

2. **Config option:** Add `display.platforms.telegram.group_busy_isolation: true` (default: false). When enabled, group busy handlers only interrupt for messages from the same user whose message triggered the current task. Other users' messages are queued.

3. **Simplest fix:** A `display.platforms.telegram.group_busy_mode` config that overrides `busy_input_mode` only for Telegram group chats, defaulting to `queue` while DMs keep `interrupt`.

**Implementation note:** The adapter-level wrapping (option 1) is the architecturally clean approach since `_should_process_message` is a `TelegramAdapter`-specific method and is not accessible at the gateway `GatewayRunner` level. The `_handle_active_session_busy_message` at `gateway/run.py` L4122 operates on `MessageEvent` objects and has no access to per-platform message filtering logic.

### Alternatives Considered

1. **Global `display.busy_input_mode: queue`** — degrades DM experience where interrupt is expected
2. **Document as "known behavior"** — groups remain nearly unusable for multi-user scenarios
3. **Per-user session keys** — larger refactor: change session key to include user_id for group chats, creating truly isolated sessions. Cleanest but biggest change.

### Feature Type

- [x] Gateway / messaging improvement

### Scope

- [x] Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

### Debug Report (optional)

（run `hermes debug share` before submitting to provide evidence of the interrupt behavior）

### Contribution

- [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR

# Bug Report: Email adapter fails with `nodename nor servname` despite valid IMAP host/credentials

---

**Summary**

Hermes email adapter fails to connect to `imap.mail.me.com:993` immediately after initialization with `[Errno 8] nodename nor servname provided, or not known`, even though the same host resolves and connects successfully outside the Hermes gateway process.

**Environment**

- Hermes Agent version: `0.16.0` (from `/Users/bobele/.hermes/hermes-agent/pyproject.toml`)
- macOS 26.5.1
- Python 3.11.15
- Config: `gateway.platforms.email.enabled = true`

**Email config**

- Address: `hermesbobele@iCloud.com`
- IMAP host: `imap.mail.me.com`
- IMAP port: `993`
- SMTP host: `smtp.mail.me.com`
- SMTP port: `587`
- Credentials: set via `hermes gateway setup`

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Run `hermes gateway setup` and configure Email with iCloud credentials.
2. Set `gateway.platforms.email.enabled = true`.
3. Restart gateway: `hermes gateway restart`.
4. Observe logs: `~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log`

**Expected behavior**

Adapter connects to IMAP, logs in, and begins polling `INBOX`.

**Actual behavior**

```

2026-06-20 12:16:43,515 INFO gateway.platforms.email: [Email] Adapter initialized for hermesbobele@iCloud.com
2026-06-20 12:16:43,515 INFO gateway.run: Connecting to email...
2026-06-20 12:16:43,517 ERROR gateway.platforms.email: [Email] IMAP connection failed: [Errno 8] nodename nor servname provided, or not known
2026-06-20 12:16:43,518 WARNING gateway.run: ✗ email failed to connect

```

This repeats on every reconnect attempt.

**Additional evidence**

- `socket.getaddrinfo('imap.mail.me.com', 993, socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)` returns valid IPv4 addresses.
- `python3 -c "import imaplib; imaplib.IMAP4_SSL('imap.mail.me.com', 993)"` connects successfully outside Hermes.
- `dig`/`host` resolve the hostname correctly.
- `nc -zv $(dig +short imap.mail.me.com | head -n 1) 993` succeeds.
- `hermes config show` does **not** list Email under Messaging Platforms, despite `.env` containing valid `EMAIL_*` variables.

**Possible cause**

The email adapter may be passing the hostname with unexpected formatting/whitespace, or there is a resolver mismatch specific to the gateway process at adapter init time.

**Request**

Please investigate why `imaplib.IMAP4_SSL(self._imap_host, self._imap_port)` raises `[Errno 8] nodename nor servname` inside the Hermes gateway when the same call works in a standalone Python REPL with identical environment variables.

items.title: [Bug]: Cmd/Ctrl+Z skips paste in desktop composer — pastes have no contentEditable undo entry
items.body:
### Bug Description

In the Hermes Desktop chat composer's `contentEditable` input, pressing Cmd/Ctrl+Z after a paste undoes the typed characters that came *before* the paste, instead of undoing the pasted text itself.

Sequence:

1. Type `Hello ` (caret at end)
2. Cmd+V to paste `world` from the clipboard (composer now contains `Hello world`)
3. Cmd+Z

Observed: composer contents go back to `Hello ` — the typed space is undone. (Or worse, a longer typed prefix is unwound, depending on how many keystrokes the user's undo stack had buffered.)

Expected: the first Cmd+Z should remove the paste, restoring `Hello ` only after a *second* Cmd+Z (the typical web/textarea expectation).

This is reproducible with the default `pbcopy`/`pbpaste` flow on macOS, with right-click → Paste, and with the Edit menu's Paste. The same behavior shows on Windows (Ctrl+Z) inside the Electron renderer.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop and focus the chat composer.
2. Type `Hello ` (or any short string).
3. Copy some other text (e.g. `world`) to the clipboard.
4. Click into the composer and press Cmd+V (Ctrl+V on Windows).
5. Press Cmd+Z once.

### Expected Behavior

A single Cmd+Z removes the pasted text, so the composer goes from `Hello world` to `Hello `. The next Cmd+Z removes the space the user typed.

### Actual Behavior

The first Cmd+Z removes the typed space (or some other typed character from before the paste), leaving `Helloworld` or similar. Pressing Cmd+Z again eventually cycles back through the rest of the typed keystrokes, but the paste is never undoable — Cmd+Z skips over it entirely.

### Affected Component

- Other

(Desktop app — `apps/desktop/`, the chat composer. None of the listed components map cleanly; the bug is in the desktop Electron renderer, not the CLI or gateway.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

- N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```
N/A — this is a pure renderer/UI bug with no gateway, agent, or runtime state involved. The reproducer is a keyboard interaction inside a `contentEditable` div in the Electron renderer. `hermes debug share` only uploads gateway/CLI logs and won't capture anything relevant. The full reproduction requires only the Desktop app focused on the chat input.
```

### Operating System

macOS 26.5.1 (also reproducible on Windows 11 — both use Electron/Chromium and the same `contentEditable` paste handler)

### Python Version

N/A (renderer-side JS/TS, no Python involved)

### Hermes Version

Desktop 0.17.0 (current main, `92d40c255 chore(release): add IamSanchoPanza to AUTHOR_MAP`)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

N/A — no exception is thrown. The handler succeeds and mutates the DOM; the problem is only that the mutation isn't recorded by the contentEditable undo manager.

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The regression was introduced in PR #45812 (commit `0a865e594`, merged 2026-06-13) as a large-paste performance fix.

The custom paste path lives in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/index.tsx`. The relevant handler:

```ts
const handlePaste = (event: ClipboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
  // ... image/data-URL short-circuits ...

  event.preventDefault()
  insertPlainTextAtCaret(event.currentTarget, pastedText)   // <-- direct DOM mutation
  flushEditorToDraft(event.currentTarget)
}
```

`insertPlainTextAtCaret` is defined in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/rich-editor.ts` and mutates the DOM directly via `range.deleteContents()` + `range.insertNode(fragment)`. The original PR comment explains the rationale: Chromium's `Editor::InsertText` (what `execCommand('insertText')` calls) is ~O(n²) on multiline blobs.

The trade-off that PR didn't flag: direct DOM mutation bypasses Blink's editing pipeline entirely, and **Blink's contentEditable undo manager only records changes that go through the editing pipeline** — i.e. native keystrokes, native paste, and `execCommand('insertText')`. The synthesized `InputEvent` from a direct `range.insertNode` does *not* create an undo entry. So:

- Before the PR: `execCommand('insertText', false, pastedText)` was used → undo entry created, Cmd+Z worked correctly (slow on huge pastes).
- After the PR: `range.insertNode(fragment)` is used → no undo entry, Cmd+Z skips the paste (fast on huge pastes).

A `dispatchEvent(new InputEvent('input', { inputType: 'insertText', data: pastedText }))` after the DOM mutation does **not** fix this — Chromium's undo manager only honors edits that flow through its own pipeline, not synthesized `InputEvent`s.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Threshold the paste handler. A new `pastePlainTextIntoEditor` helper in `rich-editor.ts` branches on `text.length <= LARGE_PASTE_THRESHOLD_CHARS` (4096, well above typical paste sizes and well below the 47 KB / 122-paragraph case from the original PR's profiling):

- **Small focused paste**: route through `document.execCommand('insertText', false, text)` → goes through Blink's editing pipeline → undo entry is created → Cmd+Z reverts the paste. This is exactly what the code did before PR #45812.
- **Unfocused editor**: fall back to `insertPlainTextAtCaret` (we can't safely `execCommand` against a selection that lives elsewhere on the page).
- **Oversized paste**: fall back to `insertPlainTextAtCaret` to keep the O(n²) freeze fix from the original PR. Trade-off: pathological pastes remain invisible to Cmd+Z, but they already freeze the UI so this is acceptable.

A PR for this is incoming on the same branch. Tests cover all three branches.

### Bug Description

### Summary

When using Perplexity's API as a custom provider, Hermes always injects tool definitions into the API request. Perplexity's models reject these, making the integration non-functional. There is currently no config option to disable tool calling on a per-provider basis.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)
- Platform: Agent37 hosted container
- Provider: custom endpoint (`https://api.perplexity.ai`)
- Model(s): `sonar`, `sonar-pro`

### Notes

- The API key is valid — the errors are capability / schema rejections, not auth failures.
- Perplexity's `sonar` model already has built-in web search, so Hermes tools are not needed for this use case.
- `sonar-pro` appears to have some tool support, but the tool schema Hermes sends does not match Perplexity's expected format.
- A per-provider `disable_tools` option would also be useful for other backends that either:
  - Lack tool / function calling support entirely, or
  - Implement a non-OpenAI-compatible tool schema.

### Steps to Reproduce

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Add Perplexity as a custom provider in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:

   ```yaml
   custom_providers:
     - name: Perplexity
       base_url: https://api.perplexity.ai
       api_key: <redacted>
       api_mode: chat_completions
       model: sonar
   ```

2. Run:

   ```bash
   hermes chat -q "test" --provider custom:Perplexity -m sonar
   ```

### Expected Behavior

### Expected Behavior

Hermes should provide a way to disable tool calling for providers that do not support it or have incompatible tool schemas. For example:

- A config option on the custom provider entry, e.g.:

  ```yaml
  custom_providers:
    - name: Perplexity
      base_url: https://api.perplexity.ai
      api_key: <redacted>
      api_mode: chat_completions
      model: sonar
      disable_tools: true
  ```

- Or a CLI flag like `--no-tools` / `--tools=off` that ensures no tool definitions are included in the request payload.

When tool calling is disabled for a provider, Hermes should not include any tool definitions in the outbound API request.

### Actual Behavior

### Observed Behavior

- With `sonar`:
  - `HTTP 400: Tool calling is not supported for this model`

- With `sonar-pro`:
  - `HTTP 400: Tool parameters must be a JSON object.`

Additional notes:

- Passing `-t ''` (empty toolset) does not resolve the issue — Hermes still sends tool definitions in the request.
- Adding `disable_tools: true` to the custom provider config entry has no effect.

This effectively prevents using Perplexity models as a Hermes custom provider.

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

Telegram

```shell
Report: https://paste.rs/F6pYy
agent.log: https://paste.rs/NOZg3
```

Python 3.11.2

Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)


### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

Hermes always includes tool definitions in every outbound API request, regardless of the provider being called. This is hardcoded into the agent's request pipeline with no mechanism to opt out on a per-provider basis.

Why it breaks Perplexity:
Perplexity's API is OpenAI-compatible but diverges in one key area — its models have strict rules around tool calling:

sonar — does not support tool calling at all → rejects any request that includes tool definitions with HTTP 400: Tool calling is not supported for this model
sonar-pro — has partial tool calling support but expects a stricter JSON schema for tool parameters than what Hermes currently sends → rejects with HTTP 400: Tool parameters must be a JSON object

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Add a disable_tools option to custom provider config entries that prevents Hermes from including tool definitions in the API request for providers that don't support them.

For example, in ~/.hermes/config.yaml:

    base_url: https://api.perplexity.ai

---
title: "Dashboard freeze: CPU 100% when context compression runs → Desktop client timeout"
labels: "bug, dashboard, context-compression"
---

## Summary

The Dashboard process (port 9119) hangs with CPU at 100% when context compression is triggered, causing the Electron desktop client to lose connection. The `launchd KeepAlive` does not restart the process because it has not exited — only become unresponsive.

## Environment

- macOS (Darwin), Hermes v0.17.0 (2026.6.19)
- Python 3.11.11
- Model: MiniMax-M2.7 (minimax-cn)
- Dashboard started via `hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119 --insecure --no-open --skip-build`
- Running under `launchd` with `KeepAlive: true`

## Symptom

- Desktop client shows: `Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms`
- Dashboard process at 99% CPU, unresponsive
- `curl http://localhost:9119/api/status` times out
- `kill` + restart recovers

## Root Cause

**`ContextCompressor.compress()` calls `call_llm()` synchronously in the main event loop without a hard timeout.**

### Call chain

```
turn_context.py:314  for _pass in range(3):
                       messages, active_system_prompt = agent._compress_context(...)
    │
    ▼
context_compressor.py:1514  response = call_llm(**call_kwargs)
                               ↓ synchronous blocking call
auxiliary_client.py:5168  def call_llm(...)
```

1. `call_llm()` for compression has a 30s default timeout (`_DEFAULT_AUX_TIMEOUT = 30.0`)
2. If the MiniMax API is slow (rate limit, cold start, network latency), the call blocks longer than 30s
3. `httpx` timeout may not cover "time to first byte" in all conditions
4. The synchronous call blocks the entire Dashboard/Gateway event loop — no other requests can be serviced
5. `launchd KeepAlive` only restarts on process exit, not CPU-bound hangs

### Evidence

`dashboard.error.log` (repeated hundreds of times):
```
⚡ Interrupted during API call.
📦 Preflight compression: ~105,228 tokens >= 102,400 threshold.
🗜️ Compacting context — summarizing earlier conversation so I can continue...
```

`gateway-exit-diag.log` — 55 non-zero exits in 37 days, with patterns of rapid restarts (<30s between starts), indicating crash loops triggered by compression hangs.

## Suggested Fixes

### Fix 1 — Hard overall timeout on compression `call_llm()`

The 30s timeout in `_get_task_timeout("compression")` is not a hard overall deadline. Consider either:
- Reducing `_DEFAULT_AUX_TIMEOUT` from 30s to 15s
- Adding a `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` with explicit `future.result(timeout=...)` so the deadline is enforced even if the HTTP library retries

### Fix 2 — Run compression in a thread/executor (non-blocking)

`context_compressor.py:1514` calls `call_llm()` synchronously in the main event loop. If this call hangs, the whole process hangs.

```python
import concurrent.futures

with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as executor:
    future = executor.submit(call_llm, **call_kwargs)
    try:
        response = future.result(timeout=30)
    except concurrent.futures.TimeoutError:
        # Fall back to dropping middle messages without summary
        return None
```

This pattern is already used elsewhere in Hermes for async tool execution.

### Fix 3 — Process-level watchdog for Dashboard

`launchd KeepAlive` only detects exits, not CPU-bound hangs. A separate watchdog script (via `launchctl`) that monitors Dashboard's CPU usage and calls `launchctl bootout` if CPU > 85% for > 90s would auto-recover without requiring manual intervention.

## Reproduction

1. Open a long-lived conversation with >100K tokens of context
2. Send a new user message
3. Dashboard CPU spikes to 100% — process becomes unresponsive
4. Desktop client: `Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms`

Frequency: every few days with active conversation history.

## Questions

1. Is the synchronous `call_llm()` in `context_compressor.py:1514` intentional, or was it meant to run in a separate thread?
2. Is the 30s compression timeout intentional for a summarization call that processes 100K+ tokens?
3. Is there a reason the Dashboard has no process watchdog beyond `launchd KeepAlive`?

## Problem
Outbound Photon/iMessage messages could still render a white square/tofu artifact during streaming. In practice it showed up as the streaming cursor/placeholder being displayed inside otherwise normal assistant replies.

This was visible in user-facing iMessage bubbles and was not limited to markdown formatting.

## Root cause
Photon was being treated like a normal streamed platform, so interim updates could include the streaming cursor. On iMessage, that cursor rendered as a visible white box artifact.

## Fix
Make Photon outbound **buffer-only / plain-text-only**:
- suppress the streaming cursor for Photon
- avoid progressive streaming bubbles on Photon
- only deliver the final plain-text message

This also keeps Photon away from rich-text/markdown paths that can leak placeholder characters into the outbound payload.

## Verification
Targeted regression tests passed after the change, including Photon and stream-consumer coverage.

## Notes
This is related to the earlier Photon/iMessage formatting issue, but the concrete bug here is the streaming cursor/tofu artifact.,timeout:60

Possible fix: unify the data source for both indicators, or have the Spawn tree subscribe to the same agent registry that feeds the status bar count.

# Telegram: sendRichMessageDraft + fresh_final_after_seconds causes N× duplicate delivery of a single table-rich response

## Summary

On a Telegram **private DM**, a single long response containing **Markdown tables** is delivered **~18 times** as separate visible messages, all containing the same content. The user sees the bot spam the same reply repeatedly instead of one animated preview + one final message.

The duplication disappears when `streaming.transport` is set to `edit` (edit-in-place) instead of `auto` (draft-based).

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: `v2026.6.19` (commit `2bd1977d8`)
- python-telegram-bot: 22.6+
- Telegram Bot API: 10.1 (Rich Messages enabled)
- Chat type: **private DM**
- Config:
  ```yaml
  streaming:
    enabled: true
    transport: auto          # draft-based streaming
    edit_interval: 0.8
    buffer_threshold: 24
    cursor: " ▉"
    fresh_final_after_seconds: 60.0   # ← key trigger
  platforms.telegram.extra.rich_messages: true   # default
  ```

## Reproduction

1. Use default config (`streaming.transport: auto`, `rich_messages: true`, `fresh_final_after_seconds: 60.0`)
2. Send the bot a request that produces a **long response (>4000 chars) containing Markdown pipe tables** — e.g. a GitHub repo briefing with multiple `| col | col |` tables
3. The response takes >60 seconds to generate (exceeding `fresh_final_after_seconds`)
4. Observe: the user receives **~18 separate messages**, each containing the full or partial response, instead of one animated preview that resolves into one final message

## What I observe

Gateway log for the affected turn (response = 5681 chars, time = 87s):

```
2026-06-20 22:55:23  inbound: msg='https://github.com/chopratejas/headroom'
2026-06-20 22:55:43  clarify button resolved: choice='Read it'
2026-06-20 22:56:50  Suppressing normal final send: final delivery already confirmed (streamed=True previewed=False content_delivered=True)
2026-06-20 22:56:50  response ready: time=87.0s api_calls=5 response=5681 chars
```

The user then replied:

> You sent this message for 18 times, fix this shit

No flood-control warnings or overflow-split warnings appear in the log for this turn — the 18 messages were sent cleanly at the Bot API level (all HTTP 200).

## Suspected root cause

Two interacting paths combine to produce the duplication:

### 1. `sendRichMessageDraft` frames rendered as separate messages

With `transport: auto` + `rich_messages: true`, the stream consumer routes mid-stream frames through `sendRichMessageDraft` (Bot API 10.1). Each frame reuses the same `draft_id` and is supposed to animate a single preview in place. However, on some Telegram clients (see #48841 — Telegram Desktop does not render `sendRichMessageDraft` correctly), each draft frame is rendered as a **separate persistent message** instead of an animated overlay.

With a 5681-char response over 87 seconds, `buffer_threshold: 24` and `edit_interval: 0.8` produce roughly **15–20 draft frames** — matching the ~18 duplicates the user observed.

### 2. `fresh_final_after_seconds: 60.0` adds one more copy

The response took 87s (>60s), so `_should_send_fresh_final()` returns True in `stream_consumer.py` (`_send_or_edit`, line ~1421). The fresh-final path sends a new `sendRichMessage` and attempts to delete the old preview. But draft frames have no real `message_id` to delete, so the cleanup may silently no-op, leaving all draft-rendered messages visible plus the fresh final.

The `prefers_fresh_final_streaming()` method on the Telegram adapter returns `False` (line 1064), which should prevent fresh-final — but `_should_send_fresh_final()` (the time-based path) bypasses that preference check:

```python
# stream_consumer.py ~line 1421
if (
    finalize
    and (
        self._should_send_fresh_final()       # ← time-based, bypasses prefers_fresh_final
        or self._adapter_prefers_fresh_final(text)
    )
    and await self._try_fresh_final(text, ...)
):
    return True
```

## Workaround

Setting `streaming.transport: edit` eliminates the draft frames and stops the duplication. Streaming is still enabled (progressive `editMessageText`), just without the draft animation layer.

```yaml
streaming:
  transport: edit
  fresh_final_after_seconds: 0.0
```

## Expected behavior

One of:
- `sendRichMessageDraft` frames should animate a single preview on all Telegram clients, OR
- The adapter should detect when draft frames are being rendered as separate messages and fall back to edit-based streaming, OR
- `fresh_final_after_seconds` should not trigger fresh-final when the preview was draft-based (no `message_id` to clean up), since the cleanup is a no-op and the fresh send just adds another visible copy

## Related issues

- #48841 — Telegram Desktop does not render `sendRichMessageDraft` streams
- #47048 — Rich-message final reply overlaps streamed legacy MarkdownV2 message
- #46515 — `sendRichMessageDraft` works but final message falls back to MarkdownV2 (`expect_edits` kills rich path)
- #49137 — Streaming preview shows table but final falls back to bullet list

The 18× duplication symptom is distinct from these: the entire response (not just the table) is multiplied, and the multiplication count matches the number of draft frames, not just a double-render.

## Summary

`hermes auth add anthropic` fails at the token-exchange step with a 404, so a fresh Claude Pro/Max OAuth login can never complete:

```
Token exchange failed: HTTP Error 404: Not Found
Anthropic OAuth login did not return credentials.
```

## Root cause

Anthropic migrated the OAuth **token** endpoint to `platform.claude.com`. The codebase is inconsistent about this:

- **Login** path — `agent/anthropic_adapter.py`, `run_hermes_oauth_login_pure()` — hardcodes the legacy host via the module constant:
  ```python
  _OAUTH_TOKEN_URL = "https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token"   # now 404s
  ```
- **Refresh** path — same file (~lines 997–1000) — already does the right thing, trying the new host first and the legacy host as a fallback:
  ```python
  token_endpoints = [
      "https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token",
      "https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token",
  ]
  ```

So token *refresh* works (which is why credentials created before the migration keep working), but a fresh *login* 404s. `hermes_cli/web_server.py` imports the same `_OAUTH_TOKEN_URL` for the dashboard OAuth flow, so the web login path has the identical bug.

## Evidence

A bare `POST` of the token request to each host:

| Endpoint | HTTP |
|---|---|
| `console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token` | **404** (dead) |
| `platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token` | **400** (live — rejects the dummy code, i.e. reachable) |

Reproduced on `v0.17.0`; the constant is still `console.anthropic.com` on current `main`.

## Suggested fix

Point the login token exchange at the live host. Cleanest is to make the login path reuse the same fallback list the refresh path already uses, rather than a single hardcoded constant:

```python
_OAUTH_TOKEN_URL = "https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token"
```

Keep `_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI` on `console.anthropic.com/oauth/code/callback` — it's the registered callback for this `client_id`, so changing it would trigger `redirect_uri_mismatch`. Only the token host is wrong.

items.title: [Bug]: WhatsApp bridge path off-by-one in plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py — parents[2] resolves one level too shallow on editable/source installs

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

On a current **editable / git source install** (`v0.17.0`, upstream `92d40c25`), the WhatsApp gateway fails to start with a non-retryable fatal error:

```
WARNING hermes_plugins.whatsapp_platform.adapter: [Whatsapp] Bridge script not found: /usr/local/lib/hermes-agent/plugins/scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js
WARNING gateway.run: ✗ whatsapp failed to connect
```

The adapter looks for the bridge at `plugins/scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js`, but the bridge actually ships at `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js` (repo root). It's a simple off-by-one in the `parents[...]` index.

### Root Cause

`plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py`:

```python
# line ~265
_DEFAULT_BRIDGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "scripts" / "whatsapp-bridge"
```

The adapter lives at `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py` — **three** directories below the repo root:

| index | path |
|-------|------|
| `parents[0]` | `plugins/platforms/whatsapp` |
| `parents[1]` | `plugins/platforms` |
| `parents[2]` | `plugins`  ← current (wrong) → `plugins/scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js` ❌ |
| `parents[3]` | repo root ← correct → `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js` ✅ |

The adapter was evidently relocated one level deeper (into `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/`) at some point, but the `parents[2]` index was not bumped to match. The pairing/install code in `hermes_cli/main.py` (`project_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` → `scripts/whatsapp-bridge`) resolves the **correct** path, so install and runtime disagree.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Editable/source install of v0.17.0.
2. Enable WhatsApp (`WHATSAPP_ENABLED=true`), bridge present at `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js`.
3. Start the gateway → `whatsapp_bridge_missing` fatal, WhatsApp never connects.

### Expected Behavior

Adapter resolves the bridge at the repo-root `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/` and connects.

### Fix

One-line change in `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py`:

```diff
-    _DEFAULT_BRIDGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "scripts" / "whatsapp-bridge"
+    _DEFAULT_BRIDGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "scripts" / "whatsapp-bridge"
```

Verified locally — after the change, `_DEFAULT_BRIDGE_DIR` resolves to `<repo>/scripts/whatsapp-bridge`, and the gateway logs `✓ whatsapp connected`.

### Relationship to #39980

PR #39980 touches this same `parents[2]` expression but is scoped to **packaged (wheel/sdist) installs** and its description explicitly notes *"WhatsApp worked in editable/git checkouts."* That premise no longer holds: after the adapter moved into `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/`, editable/source installs are broken too. The robust fix proposed there — a layout-independent `get_bundled_whatsapp_bridge_dir()` helper wired into all resolution sites — would also cover this case, so this could be folded into #39980 rather than fixed with the one-liner above. Filing separately to document the editable-install regression with a concrete repro.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.17.0 (build 2026.6.19), upstream `92d40c25`
- Python 3.11.15, Linux (editable/source install at `/usr/local/lib/hermes-agent`)
- Bridge: Baileys, present at `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js` with `node_modules/`

items.title: Windows: terminal tool creates visible bash/cmd windows that steal focus
items.body:
## Problem

On Windows, every time Hermes uses the `terminal` tool (foreground or background), it creates a visible `bash.exe` process with an associated `conhost.exe` console window. These windows flash on screen and can steal input focus.

This happens even when no conversation is active — leftover `persistent_shell` sessions (lifetime_seconds: 300) keep shells alive with visible windows after the agent finishes its task.

## Observed Behavior

- Bash/conhost windows accumulate (observed 60+ conhost.exe processes)
- Windows flash and steal focus during typing
- `wmic` process tree confirms: `python.exe → bash.exe → bash.exe (visible console)`

## Eliminated Causes (confirmed NOT the source)

- frpc.exe (already converted to hidden window)
- Windows Scheduled Tasks (cleaned up)
- Cron jobs (only run at fixed times)
- Aguoguo backend (switched to pythonw.exe)
- Gateway/Watchdog (already use pythonw.exe)

Remaining flashing confirmed as Hermes terminal sessions.

## Suggested Fix

The Windows terminal backend should use `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (0x08000000) flag when spawning bash processes. Use `pythonw.exe` instead of `python.exe` where the venv has it.

## Environment

- Windows 10, Python 3.11.4
- git-bash (MSYS2) as terminal shell
- `persistent_shell: true`, `lifetime_seconds: 300`

items.body:
## Bug Description

When the Photon sidecar (Node.js subprocess) crashes or dies for any reason, the **adapter enters a silent reconnect death spiral** with no automatic sidecar respawn. The iMessage channel stays dead until the entire Gateway is manually restarted.

## Symptom

- User sends a message through iMessage
- Sidecar processes it, but then dies
- Adapter enters an infinite reconnect loop: `[photon] inbound stream dropped (All connection attempts failed); reconnecting in 30.0s`
- The reconnect loop persists **forever** (observed for 4+ hours) at 30s intervals  
- No inbound or outbound messages get through during this period
- The adapter **never calls** `_set_fatal_error()`, so the Gateways `_platform_reconnect_watcher` never respawns the sidecar
- Platform is dead until Gateway process restart

## Root Cause Analysis

### Problem 1: Sidecar death → no respawn

The `_inbound_loop` (`adapter.py:387-425`) is the only consumer of the sidecars HTTP `/inbound` stream. When the sidecar process dies:

1. The HTTP connection drops with `peer closed connection without sending complete message body`
2. `_inbound_loop` catches the exception at line 417 and enters its reconnect loop with exponential backoff (1s → 2s → 4s → ... → 30s cap)
3. Since the sidecar process is DEAD, every reconnect attempt fails with `All connection attempts failed`
4. The loop **keeps retrying indefinitely at 30s intervals** — no escalation

The critical bug: the error handler at lines 417-425 simply logs and retries. It does NOT:
- Call `_set_fatal_error()` to alert the Gateway
- Call `_start_sidecar()` to respawn the process
- Set any state that would trigger the Gateways reconnect watcher

The Gateways `_platform_reconnect_watcher` (`run.py:6177`) is never triggered because the adapter is still registered in `self.adapters` (the Gateway thinks it is connected). There is no mechanism anywhere that monitors the sidecar process health independently.

### Problem 2: Sidecar crash logs lost

The `_supervise_sidecar` task (`adapter.py:828-841`) only pumps sidecar stdout/stderr into `logger.info()`. At default log levels (WARNING+), these logs never appear — sidecar crash details are invisible.

When the sidecar process dies:
- `_supervise_sidecar` reads EOF on the pipe at line 838 and exits silently
- The sidecars final error output is lost
- No ERROR or WARNING is ever emitted about the unexpected sidecar exit

## Impact

- **User-affecting**: iMessage channel becomes completely unresponsive until manual Gateway restart
- **Silent failure**: No error message to user, no log escalation, no metrics change
- **Complete loss of service**: Both inbound AND outbound are dead, since both route through the same sidecar

## Code References

**Adapter** — [`plugins/platforms/photon/adapter.py`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/plugins/platforms/photon/adapter.py):
- `_inbound_loop`: lines 387-425 — reconnect loop that never escalates on terminal failures
- `_supervise_sidecar`: lines 828-841 — silently exits on sidecar death

**Gateway** — [`gateway/run.py`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/gateway/run.py):
- `_handle_adapter_fatal_error`: lines 3397-3447 — only triggers if `_set_fatal_error()` is called
- `_platform_reconnect_watcher`: lines 6177-6237 — never sees fatal error, so never reconnects

**Sidecar** — [`plugins/platforms/photon/sidecar/index.mjs`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/plugins/platforms/photon/sidecar/index.mjs):
- Lines 714-731: graceful shutdown handler
- Lines 751-756: `unhandledRejection` handler (logs but does not exit)

## Proposed Fix

The `_inbound_loop` should detect terminal failures (persistent `All connection attempts failed`, i.e. the sidecar not listening) and either:
a) Call `_set_fatal_error(retryable=True)` to trigger the Gateways reconnect watcher (which creates a fresh adapter + new sidecar), OR
b) Self-heal by calling `_start_sidecar()` directly to respawn the process, then reconnect.

Additionally:
- `_supervise_sidecar` should log at WARNING level when the sidecar process exits unexpectedly (capturing its return code)
- Consider adding a sidecar health check that detects a dead process independently of the inbound stream

## Environment

- Hermes v0.17.0 (2026.6.19, upstream 2ab09a6c)
- VPS: Ubuntu 24.04, 1GB RAM
- Sidecar runs via Node.js as a subprocess

items.body:
## Bug Description

The Kanban board columns have no horizontal scrollbar on viewports narrower than the total column width (~1740px+). Users must resize the browser window to 2400+ pixels wide to see all columns, or manually scroll using trackpad gestures that aren't discoverable.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Hermes Dashboard and navigate to the Kanban board page
2. Ensure the browser window is at a typical width (e.g. 1440px or 1920px)
3. Observe: the rightmost columns (done, archived) and trash zone are clipped off-screen with no horizontal scrollbar visible
4. Resize the window to 2400px+ — all columns become visible

## Expected Behavior

A horizontal scrollbar should appear on the columns container when the total column width exceeds the viewport width, allowing users to scroll horizontally without resizing their window.

## Actual Behavior

No horizontal scrollbar appears. The `.hermes-kanban-columns` element expands to its full content width (6 columns × 280px + gaps ≈ 1740px, plus the trash zone), pushing beyond the viewport. The existing `overflow-x: auto` never triggers because the flex item's `min-width: auto` prevents it from being constrained to the parent's width.

## Affected Component

- Other

## Debug Report

N/A — this is a pure CSS layout bug with no runtime/diagnostic component.

## Operating System

macOS 26.5.1

## Root Cause Analysis

The `.hermes-kanban-columns` element (`style.css:65`) is a flex item inside `.hermes-kanban` (`display: flex; flex-direction: column`). The CSS spec defines `min-width: auto` as the default for flex items, which computes to the content-based minimum size. Since each column has `flex: 0 0 280px` (not shrinkable), the columns container's min-content width is the sum of all columns plus gaps — wider than most viewports. This prevents `overflow-x: auto` from ever producing a scrollbar.

File: `plugins/kanban/dashboard/dist/style.css`, line 65-70.

## Proposed Fix

Add `min-width: 0` to `.hermes-kanban-columns`. This is the standard CSS fix for this class of flex overflow bug — it allows the flex item to shrink below its content width, enabling `overflow-x: auto` to produce a working horizontal scrollbar.

items.body:
### Bug Description

`voice.beep_enabled` can be disabled with a YAML boolean `false`, but quoted false-like strings such as `"false"`, `"0"`, and `"off"` are currently treated as enabled.

This happens because the voice beep config is coerced with raw Python truthiness:

```python
bool(voice_cfg.get("beep_enabled", True))
```

Any non-empty string is truthy in Python, so users who quote config values can still hear voice start/stop beeps even though the config appears disabled.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes with:
   ```yaml
   voice:
     beep_enabled: "false"
   ```
2. Start CLI voice mode or call the voice beep config path.
3. Observe that beeps are still considered enabled.

### Expected Behavior

Quoted false-like values such as `"false"`, `"0"`, and `"off"` should disable voice beeps, matching other Hermes config boolean parsing behavior.

### Actual Behavior

Quoted false-like values are treated as enabled because non-empty strings are truthy in Python.

### Affected Component

- CLI (interactive chat)
- Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Debug Report

N/A - minimal config parsing bug reproduced with unit tests.

### Operating System

macOS

### Python Version

Local development Python environment

### Hermes Version

main

### Root Cause Analysis

The affected code paths use raw `bool(...)` coercion for `voice.beep_enabled`. Python treats every non-empty string as `True`, including `"false"`, `"0"`, and `"off"`.

### Proposed Fix

Use the existing shared boolean parser:

```python
is_truthy_value(voice_cfg.get("beep_enabled"), default=True)
```

Add regression tests for quoted false-like values in both the CLI voice path and standalone voice loop helper.

## Problem

On the Windows desktop app, the update dialog can push its bottom action buttons below the visible window when the UI has been zoomed / text has been enlarged with `Ctrl` + `+`.

The dialog does not appear to create a vertical scrollbar, so the user can end up unable to reach the update/dismiss actions from the visible UI.

## Environment

- App: Hermes Desktop on Windows
- Observed version indicator: `v0.17.0 (+35)`
- Observed commit/hash indicator: `65561e9`
- Entry point: bottom-right update/version/hash button

1. Open Hermes Desktop on Windows.
2. Increase the UI/text size with `Ctrl` + `+`.
3. Click the bottom-right version/update indicator.
4. When the "New update available" dialog opens, look at the lower part of the modal.

## Actual behavior

The release-notes content grows vertically and the action buttons at the bottom of the update dialog can be pushed below the visible viewport. No vertical scroll affordance appears, so the buttons are effectively inaccessible.

## Expected behavior

The update dialog should remain usable at non-default zoom levels and with long release notes.

At minimum:

- The dialog should be constrained to the available viewport height.
- The release-notes/body area should scroll vertically when content exceeds the available space.
- The action footer/buttons should remain reachable, ideally fixed or sticky within the dialog.
- Keyboard focus / `Tab` navigation should still be able to reach the action buttons.

- Verify the update dialog at 100%, 125%, 150%, and 175% zoom/text scale on Windows.
- Verify with a short changelog and a long changelog.
- Verify the action buttons remain visible or reachable by scrolling.
- Verify the dialog is still usable on smaller desktop window heights.

## Related but distinct

## Bug

Desktop UI throws `Uncaught Error: Composer is not available` in the renderer console after upgrading to **v0.17.0**. The composer input becomes unresponsive on the desktop, while the TUI / CLI backend is unaffected.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop **v0.17.0** (upgraded from v0.16.0 on 2026-06-21)
- Windows 11 (Chinese locale, but error message is in English)
- Renderer asset hash: `index-C5twiiB1.js` (post-v0.17; pre-v0.17 was `index-_oDh6Cvi.js`)
- `apps/desktop/package.json` version: `0.17.0`

## How to reproduce

1. Install / upgrade to Hermes Desktop v0.17.0
2. Launch Desktop (backend boots successfully — `[boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup`)
3. The composer input throws `Composer is not available` and the input box becomes non-interactive
4. TUI / CLI works fine in parallel — only the desktop renderer is affected

## Observed (desktop.log)

```
[hermes] HERMES_DASHBOARD_READY port=54799
[hermes] [boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup
[hermes] [renderer console] Uncaught Error: Composer is not available (file:///C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/resources/app.asar/dist/assets/index-C5twiiB1.js:73)
[hermes] [renderer console] Uncaught Error: Composer is not available (file:///C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/resources/app.asar/dist/assets/index-C5twiiB1.js:73)
[hermes] 💾 Self-improvement review: Memory updated
```

- Error originates at `index-C5twiiB1.js:73`
- Two `Uncaught Error` lines emitted back-to-back, then immediately followed by a `💾 Self-improvement review: Memory updated` (suggests something on the renderer is trying to write memory and fails because Composer is unavailable)
- No stack trace in desktop.log — only the top-level `Error: Composer is not available` line is shown

## Expected

Composer input should remain interactive after upgrade. The error should not surface at all, or at most be logged as a warning rather than an uncaught error.

## Suspected cause

Likely related to the v0.17.0 composer popout work:

- `15852722d feat(desktop): pop the composer out into a draggable floating window (#49488)`
- `eed78d6eb fix(desktop): composer popout polish — peel-off placement, panels, chip editing`
- `f697c97e0 fix(desktop): keep floating composer radius consistent with docked`

The popout refactor seems to leave a code path where the Composer component instance is referenced before it has mounted, or after it has unmounted (e.g. when the floating window has been dragged away or the dock state changes). That dereference throws `Composer is not available` and the input becomes unresponsive.

## Workaround

Use the TUI / CLI (`hermes chat`) instead of the Desktop UI. Backend is unaffected.

## Impact

- Severity: medium — desktop is unusable as a chat surface, but the CLI works
- Affects: every Desktop user who upgrades to v0.17.0
- First observed: 2026-06-21 10:27 (UTC+8), immediately after upgrade

## Related

- Related composer-popout work:
  - #49588 (drag-region z-index overlay — separate but in the same area)

items.body:
## Describe the bug

When selecting **NVIDIA NIM** as the provider in Settings > Models (desktop app), the model dropdown only shows the first 50 models in alphabetical order. This hides key models including:

- **All Nemotron models** (`nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b` at position 85)
- **GLM-5.1** (`z-ai/glm-5.1` at position 120)
- **Kimi K2.6** (`moonshotai/kimi-k2.6` at position 58)
- **All 25+ llama-nemotron variants** (positions 67-101)

These models are available through the API and work fine when typed manually, but they never appear in the dropdown because the `max_models=50` cap slices them out.

## To Reproduce

1. Set `NVIDIA_API_KEY` in `~/.hermes/.env`
2. Open Hermes desktop app > Settings > Models
3. Select "NVIDIA NIM" as the provider
4. Observe the model dropdown — it contains only models A-Z up to position 50
5. GLM, Kimi, and Nemotron models are absent

## Expected behavior

The model list should surface the curated NVIDIA models from `_PROVIDER_MODELS["nvidia"]` first.

## Root cause

The chain:
1. `GET /api/model/options` > `build_models_payload(..., max_models=50)`
2. > `list_authenticated_providers()` > `cached_provider_model_ids("nvidia")`
3. > `provider_model_ids("nvidia")` > hits the "Profile-based generic live fetch" at `hermes_cli/models.py:2188`
4. > `_p.fetch_models()` calls `GET https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/models`
5. Returns 121 models in API order (roughly alphabetical by `id`)
6. `list_authenticated_providers` slices to `model_ids[:50]` — **line 1342 of `model_switch.py`**
7. All NVIDIA-nemotron models are at positions 67-101, Kimi at 58, GLM at 120 — all hidden

The curated `_PROVIDER_MODELS["nvidia"]` list (which correctly includes `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b`, `moonshotai/kimi-k2.6`, `z-ai/glm5`, etc.) is only used as a **fallback** when the live API call fails — but the API call succeeds, so the curated list is never consulted.

## Suggested fix

Option A: Sort the live API results with curated models first (then merge remaining API models below). This is the approach `openai`/`openai-api` already uses at `hermes_cli/models.py:2132-2147`.

Option B: Increase `max_models` for providers known to serve large catalogs (NVIDIA has 121, Nous has ~400).

Option C: Use `list_agentic_models("nvidia")` from `models_dev.py` which already filters to `tool_call=True` models (44 results, all fit in 50).

## Environment

- **Hermes version**: latest (git-installed)
- **OS**: macOS 26.5.1
- **Provider**: NVIDIA NIM (`NVIDIA_API_KEY` set)
- **NVIDIA API**: `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1` returns 121 models

## Workaround

Users can type the model ID directly into the model dropdown/search field — it accepts free-text input even for models not shown in the list. Or use CLI:

```bash
hermes model --provider nvidia --model nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b
```

items.title: Firecrawl keyless API is treated as unconfigured without FIRECRAWL_API_KEY
items.body:
## Summary

Firecrawl now supports **keyless** cloud usage: its REST endpoints can be called without an `Authorization` header, with 1,000 free credits/month. Hermes still treats Firecrawl cloud as unavailable unless `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`, `FIRECRAWL_API_URL`, or the Nous tool gateway is configured.

That makes fresh/no-key setups fail with a misleading config error instead of using Firecrawl's keyless API.

Firecrawl announcement: https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/firecrawl-keyless-launch

## Current behavior

With no Firecrawl key/url/gateway configured, Hermes can still select or be configured for the `firecrawl` web backend, but the provider errors as unconfigured:

```text
Web tools are not configured. Set FIRECRAWL_API_KEY for cloud Firecrawl or set FIRECRAWL_API_URL for a self-hosted Firecrawl instance.
```

Current `main` appears to hard-code the old assumption:

- `plugins/web/firecrawl/provider.py::_get_direct_firecrawl_config()` returns `None` unless `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` or `FIRECRAWL_API_URL` is set.
- `check_firecrawl_api_key()` only returns true for direct config or the managed gateway.
- `_raise_web_backend_configuration_error()` tells users cloud Firecrawl requires `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`.
- The installed Firecrawl Python SDK still raises `ValueError: No API key provided` for `Firecrawl()`, so Hermes may need a direct REST path until the SDK supports keyless construction.

## Expected behavior

Hermes should recognize Firecrawl keyless cloud mode as a valid Firecrawl configuration, at least when the user explicitly selects/configures Firecrawl, and ideally for the default Firecrawl path.

`web_search` / `web_extract` should be able to call Firecrawl cloud without an API key and without sending an `Authorization` header.

## Suggested fix

Add first-class keyless support to the Firecrawl web provider:

1. Treat Firecrawl cloud keyless mode as available when no explicit key/url/gateway is configured, or gate it behind an explicit config option if maintainers prefer opt-in behavior.
2. For no-key cloud usage, call Firecrawl REST endpoints directly without `Authorization` (or use the SDK once it supports this).
3. Preserve existing precedence:
   - `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` = authenticated cloud Firecrawl
   - `FIRECRAWL_API_URL` = self-hosted/direct Firecrawl
   - Nous tool gateway behavior unchanged
4. Update plugin/setup/status/error text so missing `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` no longer means “Firecrawl unavailable.”
5. Add tests for keyless search/extract ensuring no `Authorization: Bearer None` / empty header is sent.

## Related but not duplicates

I found related existing threads, but none for Firecrawl's new keyless API specifically:

- #40518 / #40553: fallback to DuckDuckGo when no Firecrawl key is configured. Useful fallback, but keyless means no-key Firecrawl can now be valid rather than unavailable.
- #40190 / #40192: config/env resolution for Firecrawl key/url. Separate from no-key cloud mode.
- #32159: ordered web backend failover chains. Related fallback design, not keyless Firecrawl support.

items.title: AFK-V2: #44 Intent Classifier — message → intent_class

## Summary

The V2 gateway adapter requires an `intent_class` string on every `GatewayTurn`. Currently callers must supply it manually. This issue adds a rule-based `IntentClassifier` that maps user message text to a registered intent_class string.

## Design

- Rule-based (regex patterns, no ML dependency)
- Extensible: `register(IntentRule)` to add new patterns at runtime
- Priority ordering: higher priority wins; ties broken by registration order
- Fallback: configurable `default_intent` (defaults to `"general"`)
- `make_default_classifier()` factory with sensible V2 defaults
- `classify_and_route()` helper added to gateway_adapter.py

## Files

- `hermes_v2/kernel/intent_classifier.py` (new)
- `hermes_v2/gateway_adapter.py` (add `classify_and_route`)
- `tests/v2/kernel/test_intent_classifier.py` (new)

## Acceptance

- classify() returns correct intent for research/reminder/cron/file/workflow phrases
- Falls back to default_intent when no rule matches
- Ties broken by priority, then registration order
- `classify_and_route()` end-to-end with a live Dispatcher

items.title: AFK-V2: #45 Gateway Wiring — shadow-mode V2 routing in turn loop
items.body:
## Summary

Wire `classify_and_route()` into the V1 gateway turn loop in shadow mode.
V1 still handles all responses; V2 runs in parallel for classification and tracing.

## Design

items.title: [Bug] Desktop startup can fail with "address already in use" when primary and pooled local backends cold-start concurrently

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug

Hermes Desktop can fail during local startup with `address already in use` when two backend startup paths race inside the same Electron main process. The visible result is that Desktop fails to finish booting even though the conflict was created internally by Hermes' own backend orchestration rather than by an unrelated external process.

## Reproduction

1. Set the desktop's stored active profile to a named profile rather than `default` (in my case, `builder`).
2. Launch Hermes Desktop in local backend mode.
3. Let the main process begin the normal primary backend cold start.
4. During that same startup window, allow another profile-scoped backend request to resolve `default` as a separate local profile backend.
5. Observe that both local startup paths can choose the same localhost port before either child process has actually bound it.
6. One backend then exits with `address already in use`, and Desktop startup fails or becomes flaky.

Observable failure signal from `desktop.log`:

```text
[hermes] Starting Hermes backend via Hermes ...
[hermes] Starting Hermes backend for profile "default" via Hermes ...
[hermes] ERROR:    [Errno 48] error while attempting to bind on address ('127.0.0.1', 9121): address already in use
[hermes] Hermes backend exited (1)
[hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Hermes backend exited before it became ready (1).
```

## Expected behavior

Desktop startup should not fail because two Hermes-managed local backends selected the same port. If concurrent startup of a primary backend and a pooled profile backend is valid, port allocation should be reservation-safe and deterministic.

## Root cause

The desktop startup code has two local backend startup paths:

- `startHermes()` for the primary window backend
- `spawnPoolBackend(profile, entry)` for a non-primary pooled local profile backend

Both paths use the same port-selection helper in `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs`. The old `pickPort()` logic only checked whether a port was currently available and then released it immediately, instead of reserving it until the child process had either successfully started or failed.

That creates a classic time-of-check/time-of-use race: two concurrent callers can both observe the same port as free and both choose it. The loser then crashes when its backend actually tries to bind.

A named primary profile makes this easier to trigger because the renderer initializes its active gateway profile as `default` and only later reconciles it asynchronously to the stored desktop profile. That creates a startup window where the primary backend can be starting for a named profile while another code path still requests `default`, which the main process treats as a separate pooled backend.

I have traced the source-level race and confirmed the conflicting startup paths from logs, but I have not yet fully reduced the exact early-boot renderer caller that requested `default`.

## Fix direction

The smallest correct fix appears to be:

- add an in-process port reservation mechanism shared by both local startup paths
- reserve the chosen port before spawning either backend child
- release the reservation only if spawn fails or when the child exits

A follow-up cleanup could reduce the early boot-time `default` request window, but port reservation is the root-cause fix for the collision itself.

## My environment

- Hermes Desktop `0.15.1`
- macOS
- local desktop backend mode
- stored desktop active profile: `builder`
- source checkout used for tracing: `9d71673738263e012bdcd1b9e78e8716f1fb99ac`

## Why I believe this is upstream

I do not think this is only local machine noise or just an orphan-process problem.

What I directly observed:

- the desktop log showed both startup paths in the same boot sequence
- the failure happened on a localhost port chosen by Hermes Desktop itself
- the current desktop startup code allows the primary backend path and the pooled profile backend path to use the same non-reserving port picker

My inference from that evidence is that Hermes Desktop can self-race its own local backend startup. External stale processes can make the symptom easier to hit, but they are not required for the underlying source-level race to exist.

- [x] I'd like to contribute a fix if this approach makes sense.

items.body:
# Issue: Feature Request — Pre-spawn plugin hook for delegate_task subagents

## Problem

Plugin hooks exist for `subagent_start` and `subagent_stop`, but these fire AFTER the child is already built and running. There is no way for a plugin to inspect or block a subagent spawn BEFORE it happens.

A security plugin that wants to prevent subagents from being spawned with `terminal` access has no hook to enforce that policy. By the time `subagent_start` fires, the child already has its tools and has begun execution.

## Proposed solution

Add a `pre_subagent_spawn` plugin hook that fires in `_build_child_agent()` BEFORE the child `AIAgent` is constructed. The hook receives the requested toolsets, role, goal, and child depth. Plugins can return `{"action": "block", "reason": "..."}` to prevent the spawn.

**Location:** `tools/delegate_tool.py` in `_build_child_agent()`, before `AIAgent(...)` construction.

**Infrastructure already exists:**
- `invoke_hook()` and `register_hook()` in the plugin system
- `subagent_start` / `subagent_stop` already in `VALID_HOOKS`
- The `task_completed` plugin hook (#2817) provides a pattern for adding new emission points

**Minimal implementation (~15 lines):**

```python
# Before child construction
from hermes_cli.plugins import invoke_hook
result = invoke_hook(
    "pre_subagent_spawn",
    goal=goal,
    requested_toolsets=toolsets,
    role=role,
    child_depth=child_depth,
)
if result and isinstance(result, dict) and result.get("action") == "block":
    raise RuntimeError(f"Subagent spawn blocked by plugin: {result.get('reason')}")
```

## Concrete consumer: R4 security guard plugin

A plugin that enforces toolset policy for analytical subagents:

```python
def pre_spawn_validator(goal, requested_toolsets, role, child_depth, **kwargs):
    analytical_keywords = ["review", "analyze", "research", "audit", "assess"]
    if any(kw in goal.lower() for kw in analytical_keywords):
        mutating = {"terminal", "write_file", "patch", "execute_code", "cronjob"}
        if mutating & set(requested_toolsets):
            return {"action": "block", 
                    "reason": f"Analytical subagent cannot have mutating tools: {mutating & set(requested_toolsets)}"}
    return {"action": "allow"}
```

## Related issues

- #47092 — `pre_agent_invocation` hook (broader scope — this is the delegation-specific invocation point)

- #47092 — `pre_agent_invocation` hook (broader scope — this is the delegation-specific invocation point)
- #359 — Enhanced Extension System (broader lifecycle events)
- #2817 — Plugin hook documentation gaps

## Scope note

This is deliberately scoped to a single hook with a single consumer. The broader lifecycle hook system (#359) is a larger design effort. This proposal provides one specific, demonstrated, installable use case that can ship independently.

```
messages[X].tool_calls[0] is missing a function name
```

This happens intermittently after several tool-calling rounds.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: v0.15.1 (2026.5.29)

- Models: mimo-v2.5, mimo-v2.5-pro
- Python: 3.11.15
- OpenAI SDK: 2.41.0

1. Configure hermes to use Xiaomi MiMo as provider
2. Start a multi-turn conversation that involves tool calls
3. After several tool-calling rounds, the API returns 400

## Error Log

```
ERROR agent.conversation_loop: Non-retryable client error:
Error code: 400 - {'error': {'code': '400', 'message': 'Param Incorrect',
'param': 'messages[10].tool_calls[0] is missing a function name', 'type': ''}}
```

Also observed at message indices 21, 104, 105 — the index varies.

## Analysis

The `sanitize_tool_call_arguments` function (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py:236`) repairs corrupted `arguments` JSON but does NOT check for missing/empty `function.name`. When MiMo's response format slightly deviates from OpenAI standard (e.g. returns a tool_call without a `function.name`), this gets persisted into the conversation history and eventually causes the 400 error.

The existing "Corrupted tool_call arguments repaired" warning fires for bad JSON arguments, but the missing `function.name` case silently passes through.

## Suggested Fix

Add a check in `sanitize_tool_call_arguments` (or a new sanitization pass) that validates `function.name` is present and non-empty on every tool_call. If missing, either:
- Drop the tool_call from the message
- Attempt to recover from the tool result message
